title: Who did it, and what has happened

lessons.title: અરુણે ચા પીધી (Aruṇe cā pīdhī) — a name as the doer
lessons.gloss: Arun drank tea — a name or a noun as the doer takes -e, and the verb still follows the thing

segments.text: Before the new one: say "I drank tea" and "he drank water". (mẽ cā pīdhī, teṇe pāṇī pīdhũ.) Both times the doer was a pronoun. This lesson puts a name in its place.
અરુણે ચા પીધી. Aruṇe cā pīdhī. — "Arun drank tea."
With a verb that has an object, a name or a noun that does it takes -એ (-e), the way હું becomes મેં:
After a consonant it is the sign ે; after a vowel, the letter એ. છોકરો first turns its -ો into -ા, as it does before -ને.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: the verb follows the thing

segments.text: મીરાએ પત્ર લખ્યો. Mīrāe patra lakhyo. — "Mira wrote a letter."

પત્ર is masculine, so લખ્યો. The doer leaves the ending alone; the thing sets it: મીરાએ વાર્તા લખી (Mīrāe vārtā lakhī), for a feminine story, and અરુણે પુસ્તક વાંચ્યું (Aruṇe pustak vā̃cyũ), for a neuter book.
When the thing is a person, it takes -ને, and in Gujarati the verb follows that person too:
અરુણે મીરાને જોઈ. Aruṇe Mīrāne joī. — "Arun saw Mira."
જોઈ is feminine, for Mira. Turn it round, મીરાએ અરુણને જોયો (Mīrāe Aruṇne joyo): masculine, for Arun. Some speakers say જોયું in both; this book follows the person.

segments.prompt: Say that Mira drank tea, then that Arun read a book.
acceptedResponses: mīrāe cā pīdhī; aruṇe pustak vā̃cyũ
મીરાએ ચા પીધી. અરુણે પુસ્તક વાંચ્યું.
mīrāe cā pīdhī, aruṇe pustak vā̃cyũ

feedback.correct: -e on each name, and each verb follows its thing: cā pīdhī, pustak vā̃cyũ.
feedback.incorrect: Add -e to the name, then let the thing choose the ending: cā is feminine, pustak neuter.

segments.text: "Arun drank tea"? (અરુણે ચા પીધી (Aruṇe cā pīdhī).) Why પીધી? (ચા is feminine.) "Mira wrote a letter"? (મીરાએ પત્ર લખ્યો.) Who sets the ending, Mira or the letter? (The letter.)

lessons.title: ગયો છે, ગયો હતો (gayo che, gayo hato) — has gone, had gone
lessons.gloss: has gone, had gone — the perfect and the pluperfect, the past with છે or હતો after it

segments.text: Say "he went" and "she came". (te gayo, te āvī.) Then "he was". (te hato.) Put a past and a copula side by side, and a new past appears.
અરુણ બજાર ગયો છે. Aruṇ bajār gayo che. — "Arun has gone to the market."

ગયો says he went. ગયો છે says he went and is still away: the going matters now. The છે follows the person, as in the present: હું હમણાં આવ્યો છું (hũ hamṇā̃ āvyo chũ), "I have come this moment"; અમે આવ્યા છીએ (ame āvyā chīe), "we have come".
A verb with an object keeps its doer form and follows the thing: મેં કામ કર્યું છે (mẽ kām karyũ che), "I have done the work". There the copula is છે, whoever the doer.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: had gone

segments.text: હું સ્ટેશન પહોંચ્યો, પણ ટ્રેન ઊપડી ગઈ હતી. hũ sṭeśan pahõcyo, paṇ ṭren ūpaḍī gaī hatī. — "I reached the station, but the train had left."
હતી puts the leaving further back, before another past. It follows the way હતો, હતી, હતું, હતા do:

utterances: he went. has (now): તે ગયો છે. had (before): તે ગયો હતો.
she went. has (now): તે ગઈ છે. had (before): તે ગઈ હતી.
I did the work. has (now): મેં કામ કર્યું છે. had (before): મેં કામ કર્યું હતું.
Mira drank tea. has (now): મીરાએ ચા પીધી છે. had (before): મીરાએ ચા પીધી હતી.

segments.instruction: "Arun had drunk the tea" — Aruṇe cā pīdhī hatī
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "Arun had drunk the tea" — *Aruṇe cā pīdhī hatī*]

segments.prompt: Say that Mira has gone home, then that you had done the work.
acceptedResponses: mīrā ghare gaī che; mẽ kām karyũ hatũ
મીરા ઘરે ગઈ છે. મેં કામ કર્યું હતું.
mīrā ghare gaī che, mẽ kām karyũ hatũ

feedback.correct: gaī che for Mira, now; karyũ hatũ for the work, further back.
feedback.incorrect: Mira went: gaī, then che. The work was done before: mẽ kām karyũ, then hatũ.

segments.text: "He has gone"? (તે ગયો છે.) "She had gone"? (તે ગઈ હતી.) "I have done the work"? (મેં કામ કર્યું છે.) In મીરાએ ચા પીધી હતી, why હતી? (It follows ચા.)

segments.text: In મીરાએ પત્ર લખ્યો, which word sets લખ્યો? (પત્ર.) Now the other way round: put Arun in Mira's place. Does the verb change? (No: અરુણે પત્ર લખ્યો.) Put વાર્તા in place of પત્ર? (Yes: લખી.) And "had gone", for a woman? (ગઈ હતી.)
